Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  April 6, 2023

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on April 6, 2023. Commissioner Denmon
called the meeting to order at 6:02 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Commissioner Jacob Fragoso
  - District 2, Commissioner Cynthia McLemore - District 3,
  Commissioner Christopher Beck - District 4, Commissioner Henry
  Brown - Commissioner at Large

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Sabrina Barnes  Director
  Craig Civitello  Park Maintenance Lead Worker
  Bharat Devlia  Food Services Manager
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant
  Mary Rosounet-Rouzan  Recreation Supervisor

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. It was moved by Commissioner Brown and seconded by Commissioner
McLemore that the minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on
February 2, 2023, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Brown, Fragoso, Denmon, McLemore, and Beck
Noes: None

It was moved by Commissioner McLemore and seconded by Commissioner Brown that the
minutes for the Park and Recreation Commission meeting held on March 2, 2023, be
approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
Ayes: Commissioners Brown, Fragoso, Denmon, McLemore, and Beck
Noes: None

STAFF REPORTS. Staff report recommending the Park and Recreation Commission discuss
and recommend the Park Projects Priority List for approval by the Mayor and Council
Members.

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

It was moved by Commissioner Brown and seconded by Commissioner McLemore that the
Commission hereby approves the recommendation. The motion was carried by the
following roll call vote:
Ayes: Brown, Fragoso, Denmon, McLemore, and Beck
Noes: None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORTS - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. The Park Maintenance Leader Worker, Craig
Civitello reported that for the month of March, staff completed some beautification work
in District 2 by painting the street dividers at 65th, 66th, Gay, and Long Streets. Staff
removed graffiti on the Westside of District 2; the walls facing the 405 freeway (which
we’ve done three times per week for over a month) and throughout the city’s inner
community and main streets. Our graffiti hotline is (310) 412-8739. The Park Maintenance
Division planted all new landscaping at the Crenshaw Imperial Library.

 REPORTS - RECREATION. The Recreation Superintendent, Mary Rosounet-Rouzan,
reported the following: 1) Eco Gardner Workshops, which consist of a FREE workshop to
encourage residents to learn about the multiple benefits of planting an edible garden and
a sustainable landscape design. 2) Inglewood STEM fest – 2nd Annual partnership with
Science of Sport. A free event will expose students in grades K – sixth to science,
technology, engineering, and math through unique experiences that focus on several
sports.

REPORTS - HUMAN SERVICES. The Human Services Supervisor, Bharat Devlia reported the
following: 1)Transportation: Our Senior and Disabled Transportation Program is continuing
to provide trips to critical appointments such as dialysis and doctors’ appointments as well
as leisure trips to locations in and around Inglewood and Hawthorne. Drivers as well as
passengers continue to wear facemasks during transport. 2) Senior Center Operations: The
Inglewood Senior Center started a new Social Media class that has been well received and
filled to capacity. We have another class that starts at the end of February, A Matter of
Balance which is also filled to capacity. The Voice of Experience monthly newsletter has
been re-introduced and we are currently on our third month of providing the monthly
newsletter to our seniors so they can stay informed on Senior Center happenings. To note,
the Senior Center will be closed in recognition of Cesar Chavez Day on March 31, 2023. 3)
Nutrition: We are serving approximately 350 seniors per week through home-delivered
meals for homebound seniors and congregate lunches at our Senior Center. Our Senior
Center lunchroom is set up to accommodate safe social distancing and we look forward to
continuing to provide fresh cooked meals on a daily basis to our seniors. We continue to
provide fresh produce weekly in collaboration with the Social Justice Learning Institute. 4)
The Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP) serves meals to youth 18 years old and

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

under and operates at three sites (Crenshaw Library, Rogers Park, and Darby Park). The
CACFP is on hold while we contract a food vendor. The program's hours are Monday
through Friday, providing supper from 2:30 PM - 3:30 PM and snacks from 4:30 PM - 5:00
PM. We served an average of 70 meals per day at all three sites. We hope to provide more
meals once we have a new vendor to benefit the youth of our community. 5) We are
currently working with the Inglewood Unified School District (IUSD) to reestablish the
After-School Program (ASRP) and will know in the coming weeks, which schools will
participate in the ASRP.

REPORTS - DIRECTOR. The Director, Sabrina Barnes reported on the following Capital
Improvement updates: 1) Darby Park Walking Trak bid, 2) Vincent Park Pavilions, 3) Vincent
Park Restroom Phase 1 - open. 4) Working with Clippers on a 1,000-tree donation in District
4; tree ceremony at Vincent Park; planting 50 trees around Amphitheatre.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. None

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:49 p.m.
